summary: Paul David Numrich is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies who completed his doctorate at the University of Michigan in 1992. In 2006, he held posts at Loyola University Chicago and the Theological Consortium of Greater Columbus.

Paul Debes was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Nyanatiloka Mahathera from 1931 to 1932. He founded the Buddhistisches Seminar (1948), the Buddhistische Gesellschaft Hamburg (serving on its board in 1954), and the Deutsche Buddhistische Gesellschaft (1955).

Paul Demiéville worked in Sinology and Buddhist studies, earning a degree at the Sorbonne and studying under Chavannes, Lévi, Pelliot, Meillet, and Cabaton. He held posts at EFEO, Xiamen University, Maison Franco-Japonaise, INALCO, and the Collège de France (1946–1964).

Paul Deussen was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Bonn, Tübingen, and Berlin, completing his habilitation under Eduard Zeller. He taught Sanskrit at Geneva, served as Privatdocent at Berlin, and became a professor at Kiel University in 1889.

Paul Dundas was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Edinburgh and under Michael Coulson. He led Asian studies at the University of Edinburgh (~1976–2017) and headed the Pali Text Society (~2003–2023).

Paul E. Muller-Ortega is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed his doctoral studies at the University of California, Santa Barbara. As of 2000, he taught in the Department of Religion and Classics at the University of Rochester.
Paul Ekman studied at New York University (~1952–1954) and Adelphi University (~1954–1958). He held an academic post at the University of California, San Francisco, from approximately 1960 to 2004.

Paul F. Knitter is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University (~1962–1966) and the University of Marburg (~1969–1972), later holding a post at Union Theological Seminary (~2007–2017).

Paul Fredericq was a historian who studied at Ghent University and the University of Liège, where he completed his doctorate. He served as a professor at Liège (~1879–1883) and Ghent University, where he became professor in 1883 and rector in 1919.

Paul Fuller is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his PhD at the University of Bristol under Rupert Gethin and studied under Paul Dundas. He held lectureships at the University of Sydney and Cardiff University.

Paul G. Brewster studied at Oakland City University and the University of Oklahoma. An Indologist, he taught at the University of Tennessee, UNC Chapel Hill, Shurtleff College, Henderson State University, and Tennessee Technological University (1954).

Paul G. Hackett is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as Tibetan collection curator and bibliographer at the University of Virginia (attested 1994, 2003) and later taught Classical Tibetan at Columbia University (attested 2003, 2016).

Paul Goldschmidt worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Heidelberg, Berlin, and Tübingen, and under Weber, Roth, and Theodor Benfey at Göttingen, where he earned his PhD. In 1874, he became an epigraphist for the Government of Ceylon.

Paul Greenough is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago between 1968 and 1977 and joined the history faculty at the University of Iowa in 1974.

Paul Groner is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar who earned his PhD from Yale and studied under Akira Hirakawa at the University of Tokyo. He has spent his career on the faculty at the University of Virginia (attested 1982–2026).

Paul Hacker was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Bonn, Heidelberg, Frankfurt, and Berlin (PhD). Following habilitation under Willibald Kirfel, he held chairs in Indology at the University of Bonn (1955–1963) and the University of Münster (1963–1978).

Paul Harrison is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Auckland and the Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana. He taught at Canterbury and later joined the faculty at Stanford University (~2007).

Paul Hershman was an Indology and anthropology researcher who pursued doctoral studies at the London School of Economics from approximately 1971 to 1975. He served as a Lecturer in Anthropology at the University of Sussex from 1975 to 1976.

Paul Hoornaert is a scholar working in the fields of Buddhist studies and philosophy. His career includes an attested academic appointment as a lecturer at Kanazawa University between at least 1991 and 2002.

Paul Horn was an Iranian and Central Asian studies linguist. He studied at the University of Berlin and completed his doctorate under Christian Bartholomae at Halle-Wittenberg, later serving as Privatdozent (1889) and associate professor (1900) at the University of Strasbourg.
